overview: This document presents the preliminary architectural and structural concept for a 3,000-seat church auditorium in Zimbabwe. It is compiled directly from the project’s concept model (revision PL06) and is issued so that the building committee, prospective contributors and consulting engineers can review the proposal before engineering design begins.

The building is a single long-span hall of 50 metres clear between steel portal columns, roofed by nine trusses at grid lines 3 to 11. Congregation seating is arranged in six blocks across 41 rows: a gently sloped front section, a level mid cross-aisle carrying the wheelchair band, and a uniformly tiered rear section rising to a rear platform at +4.600 m.

A two-level foyer at the entrance front, continuous ambulatories along both long sides, and a back-of-house wing behind the platform enclose the hall. All structural members in the model are space reservations or placeholder sections; no element has yet been analysed or designed.
vision: The auditorium is conceived as one room. Every seat looks toward a 20-metre-wide platform beneath a single, uninterrupted roof, so that the congregation reads itself as one body rather than a set of separate galleries.

Option A in the model — a single-level hall with a tiered rear section — was retained in preference to a floor-plus-balcony scheme. It avoids a suspended or cantilevered balcony structure and keeps the structural system to a long-span roof on columns, at the cost of a deeper hall and a maximum viewing distance of 45.45 m.

The serving spaces sit outside the column lines: ambulatories carry circulation and egress ramps along both sides, the foyer and upper foyer gather people at the entrance, and the back-of-house wing supports the platform. The structure is regular and repetitive, and the trusses are intended to remain legible from the seating.

principles.b: A single 50 m clear span; no columns or balconies within the seating.
Front slope at 1:10.56, level cross aisle at +1.150, rear tiers on a uniform 150 mm riser.
Nine repeating trusses on a 59.0 × 88.0 m grid set the rhythm of roof, walls and lighting.
Foyer, ambulatories and back-of-house sit outside the hall columns and carry all circulation.

interior: Interior views are exported from the concept model. Finishes, colours and lighting in the renders are indicative only.
structure: The primary structure is a series of nine long-span steel trusses spanning 50.000 m between hall portal columns on grid lines B and G. Trusses bear at +14.000 m and rise at 1:12.5 to an apex depth of approximately 3.3 m at grid line D–E centre.

Purlins at 5.0 m centres on plan span between trusses. Roof-plane X-bracing is placed in bays 3–4, 7–8 and 10–11, with wall bracing within the hall cavity walls in the end bays and knee braces at grid lines B and G (4–10) indicating a moment-frame concept (assumption A-27).

Lower wings — foyer, ambulatories and back-of-house — are framed on 0.40 m perimeter column reservations with their own roof beams. Foundations are shown as pad footings at every column position as reference locations only; no geotechnical information is available.

risks.finding: All truss members carry placeholder sections; the 50 m span has not been analysed for dead, live or wind load.
risks.response: Appoint structural engineer; establish loading basis and analyse primary frames.

risks.finding: All 76 footings are reference locations only; no geotechnical data exists.
risks.response: Commission site investigation before foundation design.

risks.finding: Required exit widths and travel distances in the model use a placeholder method; 527 hall positions exceed the travel flag.
risks.response: Fire engineer to confirm occupancy, exit capacity and travel limits under applicable Zimbabwean requirements.

risks.finding: Lateral stability relies on knee braces at B/G 4–10, roof bracing in three bays and cavity-wall bracing; system not verified (A-27).
risks.response: Confirm stability strategy in both directions; review brace positions.

risks.finding: Hall walls are 14.3 m high cavity walls with X-bracing in the cavity; wall and wind design not undertaken.
risks.response: Assess wall type, wind girts and connection to frame.

risks.finding: Four L02 refuge spaces modelled; protection and assisted evacuation not designed (OI-16).
risks.response: Develop refuge and evacuation-lift or assisted strategy.

risks.finding: Main LED wall 12.8 × 7.2 m and line arrays shown as allowances; rigging loads not provided.
risks.response: Obtain rigging loads; design certified rigging points.

risks.finding: Gutter, downpipe and overflow sizes not set for 4 gutters and 28 downpipes.
risks.response: Hydraulic design for catchment and rainfall intensity.

risks.finding: External stairs and ramps assume flat grade; site levels unknown.
risks.response: Topographic survey; set finished floor level.

risks.finding: 466 seats sit more than 45° off the pulpit axis; 2,046 seats rely on IMAG screens.
risks.response: Confirm acceptability with client; review screen positions.

risks.finding: Irregular bays at grid 6 (6.5 m and 9.5 m) differ from the 8.0 m typical bay.
risks.response: Confirm truss positions and purlin spans.

risks.finding: True north is not defined; level L03 (+4.300) sits below L02 (+4.600).
risks.response: Set geolocation and true north; rename or reorder levels.

recommendations: Confirm the brief: seating target, choir provision and the single-level arrangement (Option A).
Commission a topographic survey and geotechnical investigation of the site.
Appoint a structural engineer to establish the loading basis and analyse the 50 m truss frames.
Appoint a fire engineer to verify occupancy, exit widths, travel distances and refuge provisions.
Obtain AV rigging loads and MEP plant allowances before roof design is fixed.
Engage a quantity surveyor to price the measured quantities once sections are designed.

assumptions.item: Lift shaft enclosure provides no stability contribution.
Portal knee braces represent a moment-frame concept at grid lines B and G.
Entrance canopy follows the low-cost continuous option.
Refuge spaces are allowances; protection and assisted evacuation not designed.
Client decision: no extra chairs on the stage floor behind the platform.
Door operation outward in the direction of escape with panic hardware.
Site is level; external steps and ramps set for flat grade.
Steel sections follow SANS 10162-1 designation format in schedules.
